about: Thin image/video score research, 2026-10-07. Candidate rows for data/results.json, new benchmarks for data/benchmarks.json, ledger additions for data/sources.json (new entries, or {id, add_match} to add a pinned URL to an existing entry). Nothing here is imported yet. Every value was extracted by script from a file fetched in this session (local copies under the session scratchpad tv/dl/, path in evidence.local_copy) and re-checked against it, except the Datapoint Image Bench rows, which are transcribed from the leaderboard chart image in the card (evidence.transcribed_from_image = true). 'gaps' lists thin models still below 3 counted results after these rows (counted_after) and what was searched.

results.note: image_to_video, category overall, split latest; exact entry 'flux-3-video-20260811' (organization bfl); 37,042 votes; published 95% interval 1444.5–1454.4; leaderboard_publish_date 2026-09-22. results.note: Stable Diffusion v1.4 (1B); Table 5 Alignment column 0.691 (win rate among 26 HEIM models); Table 4 'Stable Diffusion v1-4' (CompVis), ref [4]; Appendix D

evidence.protocol: HEIM v1.1.0: images generated by the HEIM authors for all 26 models; Alignment aspect = text-image alignment measured by human-rated overall alignment (1-5, five MTurk annotators per sample) and CLIPScore over the alignment scenarios (MS-COCO 2014 val incl. art-style variants, CUB-200-2011, DrawBench, PartiPrompts, etc.; Tables 2-3); win rate = probability the model beats a uniformly random other model of the 26 on a metric, head-to-head (Sec. 7)
evidence.measurement_origin: explicit original benchmark-author evaluation (HEIM authors generated and scored all images)
evidence.evaluator_relationship: Stanford CRFM-led team (with Microsoft, Aleph Alpha, POSTECH, Adobe, CMU co-authors); none of these organisations made the mapped model, so independent
evidence.identity_basis: Table 4 'Stable Diffusion v1-4' (CompVis), ref [4]; Appendix D

setup.version: Rapidata/image-to-video-realism dataset card @ d7abf89 (2026-10-01): 19 participants incl. a real-footage baseline, 25 prompts with image assets, 2,981 comparisons, 522,210 human votes
setup.metric: Published 'Overall ranking' ELO over the two human leaderboards (Photorealism: 'Which video looks more like it was shot by a real camera?'; Visual integrity: 'Which video has more glitches and is more likely to be AI generated?'), prompt not shown to annotators.
setup.protocol: Head-to-head comparisons of two clips generated from the same prompt image and text; userScore-weighted crowd votes collected with the Rapidata SDK.
setup.limitations: Generation settings (resolution, duration, API endpoint) are not documented on the card; only 25 prompts. Ratings are relative to this participant pool (includes a ground-truth baseline at ~1470) and are not on Arena or other Rapidata scales. Do not mix with the Photorealism / Visual integrity sub-rankings.

benchmarks.name: Rapidata relative camera movement (I2V, alignment Elo)

setup.version: Rapidata relative-camera-movement dataset card @ e03ac78 (2026-09-29): 15 models, 50 stills, 220 hand-written scene-specific camera prompts (camera movement and perspective switching), 3,270 clips
setup.metric: Published Bradley-Terry style ELO on the Alignment leaderboard ('Which video matches the description better?', instruction shown).
setup.protocol: Each still + prompt sent to every model as an image-to-video request (still as first frame); 22-44 votes per pair (39.7 avg) from a dedicated Rapidata audience in 125 countries.
setup.limitations: Per-model resolution/duration not documented on this card. Ratings are relative to this pool and not comparable with the scene-agnostic Rapidata camera-movement Elo.

benchmarks.name: HEIM text-image alignment (aspect win rate, v1.1.0)

setup.version: HEIM v1.1.0 as summarised in arXiv 2311.04287v1 Table 5 (26-model pool)
setup.metric: Alignment aspect win rate: probability that the model outperforms another of the 26 models chosen uniformly at random, head-to-head per metric (human-rated alignment and CLIPScore) over the alignment scenarios; already 0-1.
setup.protocol: Images generated by the HEIM authors with each model; five Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators per human-rated sample; scenarios MS-COCO 2014 val (incl. art-style variants), CUB-200-2011, DrawBench, PartiPrompts and others listed in Table 2.
setup.limitations: Relative to the fixed 26-model HEIM pool (adding/removing models changes win rates); mixes human and CLIPScore metrics; 2023 checkpoints and API versions. Other aspect columns (quality, aesthetics, etc.) are not imported.

benchmarks.name: ImageReward human ranking of T2I models (#wins, real user prompts)

setup.version: ImageReward report v4 (28 Dec 2023), Table 1, Real User Prompts / Human Eval. #Win; fixed pool of 6 models
setup.metric: Aggregated human win count of each model against the other five models (raw count, higher is better); stored unscaled.
setup.protocol: Researcher annotation by the authors: 100 real-user (DiffusionDB) test prompts; each model generates 10 outputs per prompt, the best of 10 is picked, annotators rank the six models' images per prompt; #Win = aggregated win count of the model against all others (Sec. 2.3)
setup.limitations: Counts depend on the six-model pool and the number of annotations (denominator not published), so only comparable within this run; best-of-10 selection per model; early-2023 checkpoints/API.

setup.version: ImageReward report v4 (28 Dec 2023), Table 1, MS-COCO 2014 'Zero-shot FID' column, author-computed rows only
setup.metric: FID between 30k generated images and MS-COCO 2014 validation images, both at 256x256; lower is better.
setup.protocol: Zero-shot FID on 30k MS-COCO 2014 validation captions, outputs unified to 256x256, optimal classifier-free guidance chosen by grid search over [1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0] (Sec. 2.3, Table 1 caption); computed by the ImageReward authors
setup.limitations: FID correlates poorly with human preference for modern models (Spearman 0.09 to human ranking in the same table); CFG grid-searched per model; not comparable with other papers' COCO FID numbers (different resolution/guidance/reference sets).

setup.version: VVRBench main split as released with arXiv:2609.35641v1 (28 Sep 2026): 10,000 tasks, complexity 3-48, 32 constraint types
setup.metric: Task accuracy: share of tasks whose generated image passes every constraint (counts, attributes, sizes, spatial relations) under the deterministic, reference-free pixel-to-object verifier; reported in %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: VVRBench main split, 10,000 programmatically generated tasks of structural complexity 3-48 over 32 constraint types; a generated image succeeds only if every constraint passes the deterministic pixel-to-object verifier; accuracy = mean success over tasks. Open-weight models at Table 9 settings (steps/CFG); API models at medium quality 1024x1024; responses without an image count as failures.
setup.limitations: Synthetic geometric-object scenes only (precise instruction following, not aesthetics). Do not pool with VVRBench-Fast (820-task subset) or VVRBench-Challenge. Near-zero scores for weak models are at the floor.

setup.version: VVRBench-Challenge as released with arXiv:2609.35641v1: 720 tasks, complexity 45-80 (20 per integer complexity), 14 additional group-level constraint types
setup.metric: Task accuracy: share of tasks whose image passes every constraint under the deterministic verifier; %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: VVRBench-Challenge, 720 tasks of complexity 45-80 (20 per integer complexity) adding 14 group-level constraint types; same deterministic verifier and all-constraints-pass accuracy. API models only: GPT models at medium quality 1024x1024, Gemini models at 1K (Table 9); responses without an image count as failures.
setup.limitations: API models only in this report; best model 21.4%, so low scores are compressed. Separate task set from the main VVRBench split; not pooled with it.

setup.version: ChartSync as released with arXiv:2607.10301v1 (11 Jul 2026): 870 triplets, Table 2
setup.metric: Overall = equal average of OCR F1, SSIM, TESR, VLCS and BFS (each 0-100), stored /100. VLM-judged parts use Gemini-3.1-Pro at temperature 0.1.
setup.protocol: ChartSync: 870 expert-validated chart-editing triplets (9 chart categories, 4 task types, 235 geometry-coupled VLCE instances); each model edits the source chart image per instruction; Overall = equal average of five metric-level scores: OCR F1 and SSIM against the programmatic ground truth, and Gemini-3.1-Pro judged TESR (text edit success), VLCS (visuo-logical consistency, VLCE subset only) and BFS (background fidelity).
setup.limitations: Charts only (statistical-chart text and geometry edits). Mixes pixel metrics with a single VLM judge; VLCS covers only the 235 VLCE items. Metric-level summary, not a per-sample average.

setup.version: InfoEdit as released with arXiv:2609.33286v1 (27 Sep 2026): 1,000 infographics x 4 edit tasks
setup.metric: Avg. = mean over the four tasks of success rate (edit compliance AND content preservation, judged by Gemini-3.1-Pro); %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: InfoEdit: 1,000 rendered infographics (eight logical-relation families) x four reflow-requiring edit tasks (Expand-Text, Insert-Element, Swap-Block, Reshape-Canvas) = 4,000 edits; a sample succeeds (SR) only if both edit compliance and content preservation pass under the Gemini-3.1-Pro judge (validated against human majority votes, Appendix E); Avg. = mean SR over the four tasks.
setup.limitations: Infographic layouts only; single MLLM judge; most models are near the floor (0-5%), so the run mainly separates frontier models.

setup.version: PaintBench as released with arXiv:2606.00188v1 (29 May 2026), baseline visual conditions, Table 1
setup.metric: Benchmark Avg.: macro-average over 20 tasks of mean IoU (%) between the model's edit and the deterministic ground truth; stored /100.
setup.protocol: PaintBench: procedurally generated single-answer editing problems (20 task types in four categories: geometric transformation, structural manipulation, color change, symbolic reasoning) at 1024x1024 baseline conditions; deterministic pixel-level scoring of the edited image against the programmatic ground truth (mean IoU over edit classes), no judge model; Benchmark Avg. = macro-average over the 20 tasks.
setup.limitations: Synthetic shapes/colours on plain backgrounds; precise single-answer edits rather than open-ended editing quality; best model 17.1%, most near the floor.

setup.version: MechVerse test split as released with arXiv:2605.14843v1 (14 May 2026), Table 1 WorldModelBench columns
setup.metric: Sum of WorldModelBench judge scores (instruction 0-3, physics 0-5, common sense 0-2), out of 10; stored /10.
setup.protocol: MechVerse test split: image-to-video generation of mechanical assemblies (gears, linkages, cam-follower, pistons, multi-part mechanisms) from a first frame plus a structured motion prompt; default inference settings per model; outputs scored with the WorldModelBench MLLM judge: instruction following (0-3) + physics (0-5) + common sense (0-2) = Sum (0-10).
setup.limitations: MLLM judge; the authors report that judge scores rise with mechanism complexity while human-rated motion correctness falls, so the judge is lenient on part-level kinematic errors. VBench-I2V columns in the same table are separate automatic metrics and are not imported.

setup.version: Rapidata/text-to-image-human-preference-6M dataset card @ 2f602f4 (2026-10-01): 43 models, 1,514 prompts, 680,548 comparisons, 6,123,853 votes
setup.metric: Published 'Overall ranking (ELO, aggregated across all four leaderboards)': Alignment, Preference, Coherence and Text coherence human pairwise leaderboards combined.
setup.protocol: Benchmark.ai Image Benchmark run by Rapidata: 43 text-to-image models, 1,514 prompts (616 asking for rendered text), 680,548 head-to-head image pairs for the same prompt; 6.1M human votes on four questions (Alignment with prompt shown; Preference, Coherence and Text coherence without the prompt); Overall = Rapidata's published ELO aggregated across the four leaderboards. Generation settings per model are not documented on the card.
setup.limitations: Per-model generation settings (quality tier, resolution, endpoint) are not documented on the card except where encoded in the model label; ratings are relative to this 43-model pool and not on the LMArena or other Rapidata scales. Do not import the four component leaderboards separately (same comparisons).

setup.version: Rapidata/Face_Generation_Benchmark card @ c6ed7ea: 12 models, ~22,000 responses (benchmark run August/September 2025)
setup.metric: Published leaderboard 'score' (Elo-style rating from pairwise wins) for prompt alignment on descriptions of people.
setup.protocol: Rapidata Human Face Generation Alignment: 12 text-to-image models (Replicate model ids) generate images from descriptions of people; ~22,000 human pairwise responses to 'Which Image follows the description of the human better?'; published leaderboard score (Elo-style rating) with wins and total matches.
setup.limitations: Faces/people prompts only; alignment question only (no aesthetics); prompt count and generation settings beyond the Replicate model id are not documented; ratings relative to this 12-model pool.

setup.version: VideoArgus-Bench as released with arXiv:2608.05485v1 (6 Aug 2026), Table 2 T2V leaderboard
setup.metric: Mean VideoArgus score (0-10, importance-weighted criterion scores with hard-criterion caps), stored /10.
setup.protocol: VideoArgus-Bench (1,026 human-verified input instances over five tasks); every candidate video for an input is scored against the same frozen, output-blind, sample-specific rubric (generated once with Claude Opus 4.8; 6-17 criteria with importance weights and hard-criterion caps), with criterion-level evidence and judgments by Qwen3.6-27B plus visual tools; VideoArgus score 0-10 per video, averaged per model and task.
setup.limitations: Automatic rubric + VLM judge (Qwen3.6-27B), validated against 15 annotators on a separate 210-input set; one leaderboard per task, the other three tasks (TS2V, TV2V, TSV2V) are not imported. Generation settings per model not documented.

setup.version: VideoArgus-Bench as released with arXiv:2608.05485v1 (6 Aug 2026), Table 2 TI2V leaderboard
setup.metric: Mean VideoArgus score (0-10, importance-weighted criterion scores with hard-criterion caps), stored /10.
setup.protocol: VideoArgus-Bench (1,026 human-verified input instances over five tasks); every candidate video for an input is scored against the same frozen, output-blind, sample-specific rubric (generated once with Claude Opus 4.8; 6-17 criteria with importance weights and hard-criterion caps), with criterion-level evidence and judgments by Qwen3.6-27B plus visual tools; VideoArgus score 0-10 per video, averaged per model and task.
setup.limitations: Automatic rubric + VLM judge (Qwen3.6-27B), validated against 15 annotators on a separate 210-input set; one leaderboard per task, the other three tasks (TS2V, TV2V, TSV2V) are not imported. Generation settings per model not documented.

setup.version: Datapoint Image Bench overall board published 2026-08-19 (30 models, 500 prompts), as shown in the datapointai/text-2-image-human-preferences-2m card @ e1d8719
setup.metric: Overall Elo (Bradley-Terry on raw votes, equal weight per category, anchored FLUX.1 [schnell] = 1000), whole points.
setup.protocol: Datapoint Image Bench: 30 text-to-image models, 500 stress-test prompts in 10 categories (counts, typography, negation, ordering, composition), one image per prompt with a single fixed seed, prompts passed verbatim (no rewriting, no best-of-N); complete round-robin, every pair judged blind by 10 validated annotators ('Which image do you prefer?'), 2,161,160 votes; Elo from a Bradley-Terry fit on raw votes with equal category weight, anchored at FLUX.1 [schnell] = 1000, rounded to whole points.
setup.limitations: Values are printed only in the card's chart image (the vote data is gated); single seed per prompt; ratings relative to this 30-model pool. Category boards are not imported.

setup.version: Datapoint Video Bench overall board in the datapointai/text-to-video-human-preferences-326k card @ 49295b5 (2026-09-28): 15 models, 314 prompts
setup.metric: Overall Elo (Bradley-Terry on raw votes, equal weight per category, 14 original models centred at 1000); 95% rank spread kept in notes.
setup.protocol: Datapoint Video Bench: 15 text-to-video models, 314 prompts in eight categories (camera moves, physics/causality, object permanence, multi-subject interaction, human motion, legible text, stylized animation, product ads); one 1280x720 clip per model and prompt, audio stripped; full round-robin with 10 blind votes per pair ('Which video better fulfills the prompt with the highest overall quality?'), 325,520 votes; Elo from a Bradley-Terry fit on raw votes, equal weight per category, centred so the 14 original models average 1000.
setup.limitations: Audio removed, so audio-capable models are judged on video only; one clip per model and prompt; P-Video-2-Pro added in a second round against 13 models. Ratings relative to this 15-model pool.

setup.version: EvalAlign report v3 (10 Oct 2024), Table 3 'Human' column; fixed 24-model pool, 100 prompts
setup.metric: Mean human text-image alignment score per model from the EvalAlign question set (raw units; observed range 4.15-5.45), stored unscaled.
setup.protocol: EvalAlign test set: 24 text-to-image models each generate images for the same 100 prompts (2.4k images); human annotators answer the text-image alignment question set (object, count, colour, style, spatial and other skills) with fixed scoring options; 'Human' = mean human alignment score per model (raw units, higher is better).
setup.limitations: Only 100 prompts per model; absolute scale depends on the question set, so only comparable within this run. The faithfulness table (Table 2) and the automatic metric columns (EvalAlign, HPS v2, CLIPScore, ImageReward, PickScore) are not imported.

setup.version: SDXL-Lightning report v3 (2 Mar 2024), Table 2 'FID (Whole)' column
setup.metric: FID between images for the first 10K COCO validation captions and the matching COCO images, whole image resized to 299px; lower is better.
setup.protocol: Authors' FID on the first 10K MS-COCO validation captions: images generated by each model at its listed step count (1024px class models), FID-Whole = standard FID with whole images resized to 299px for InceptionV3 against the matching COCO ground-truth images; lower is better.
setup.limitations: FID tracks distribution match more than prompt following or preference; step count per model is part of the setting; not comparable with other papers' COCO FID (different subsets/resolutions). FID-Patch and CLIP columns not imported.

setup.version: Cosmos 3 report v4 (23 Jun 2026), Table 11 'UniGenBench All (1170)': original 600 UniGenBench prompts plus NVIDIA's 570 UniGenBench-Phys prompts
setup.metric: Mean testpoint accuracy (binary pass/fail per testpoint, Gemini 3.1 Pro judge) over all 1,170 prompts; %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: UniGenBench (600 prompts, 5 themes/20 subthemes, 10 primary and 27 sub-criteria) augmented by NVIDIA with 570 Physical-AI prompts (UniGenBench-Phys); Gemini 3.1 Pro judges each generated image against each testpoint (binary pass/fail); score = mean testpoint accuracy over all 1,170 prompts ('All'). Cosmos 3 images generated from upsampled JSON prompts (shift 3.0, guidance 4.0, 50 steps, Table 21).
setup.limitations: NVIDIA-specific variant of UniGenBench (added Physical-AI subset, Gemini 3.1 Pro judge), not the original UniGenBench leaderboard; NVIDIA's own model is lab-reported. The report's Table 1 overview prints 90.85 for Gemini 3 Pro Image while Table 11 prints 90.69 (Table 11 used).

setup.version: MindWorldBench as released with arXiv:2609.39147v1 (30 Sep 2026; ACM MM 2026), 744 prompts, Table 1
setup.metric: Intention Accuracy: % of prompts whose generated action matches the intention implied by the mental-state condition (binary, Gemini 3.1 Pro judge); stored /100.
setup.protocol: MindWorldBench: 744 expert-designed image-to-video prompts in which a character's mental state (belief, desire, perception) should determine one of two candidate actions; each I2V system generates one video per prompt; Gemini 3.1 Pro judges with a structured multi-step rubric pipeline (validated on 100 videos against 10 human experts); Intention Accuracy = % of prompts whose generated action follows the intention implied by the mental-state condition.
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge; the benchmark's other columns (visual quality, commonsense plausibility 1-5; world-state maintenance %) are not imported. Two candidate actions per prompt, so a model ignoring the mental state can still hit the intended action by chance.

benchmarks.name: ViGoR-Bench zero-shot visual reasoning, image models (Result Avg)

setup.version: ViGoR-Bench as released with arXiv:2603.25823v1 (26 Mar 2026), Table 3 'Result Metric (%) Avg'
setup.metric: Mean of the four Result metrics (BC, RO, VQ, RS), Gemini-2.5-Pro judge with ground-truth references; %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: ViGoR-Bench: zero-shot visual reasoning tasks (physical, knowledge and symbolic reasoning; 20 subdomains, e.g. mazes, sudoku, science phenomena) posed to image-editing/unified models (input image + instruction) and video generators (reasoning sequence, final frame scored); Gemini-2.5-Pro judges against ground-truth references (validated on a 1,080-output split against three human experts). Result Metric Avg = mean of BC, RO, VQ and RS (%).
setup.limitations: Image-editing and unified models without chain-of-thought; the CoT rows (Bagel-Think, GPT-image-1+, Nano Banana+) are other settings and not imported. Single VLM judge.

benchmarks.name: ViGoR-Bench zero-shot visual reasoning, video generators (Result Avg)

setup.version: ViGoR-Bench as released with arXiv:2603.25823v1 (26 Mar 2026), Table 3 'Result Metric (%) Avg'
setup.metric: Mean of the four Result metrics (BC, RO, VQ, RS), Gemini-2.5-Pro judge with ground-truth references; %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: ViGoR-Bench: zero-shot visual reasoning tasks (physical, knowledge and symbolic reasoning; 20 subdomains, e.g. mazes, sudoku, science phenomena) posed to image-editing/unified models (input image + instruction) and video generators (reasoning sequence, final frame scored); Gemini-2.5-Pro judges against ground-truth references (validated on a 1,080-output split against three human experts). Result Metric Avg = mean of BC, RO, VQ and RS (%).
setup.limitations: Only the final frame of each generated video is scored by the Result metric; Process metrics (whole sequence) not imported. Single VLM judge.

setup.version: PhyGround as released with arXiv:2605.10806v1 (11 May 2026), Table 2, 250 ti2v prompts
setup.metric: Overall human score on a 1-5 scale (equal weight of general adherence and physics-domain views), stored /5 with chance 0.2.
setup.protocol: PhyGround: 250 text+image-to-video prompts (first frame given; sources VideoPhy-2, Physics-IQ, OpenVid, WorldModelBench) covering 13 physics laws; each model generates one video per prompt at its native default settings (2,000 videos); 352 quality-controlled human annotators rate 1-5 semantic alignment, physical temporal validity, persistence and the applicable physics laws; Overall = equal-weight combination of the general and physics-domain views.
setup.limitations: Only 8 models; native default settings per model (resolution/fps differ); human means of 2.5-3.3 sit in a narrow band. Sub-dimension columns and the PhyJudge automatic scores are not imported.

benchmarks.name: EdiVal multi-turn editing overall (EdiVal-O after turn 3)

setup.version: EdiVal-Agent report v3 (17 Mar 2026), Table 3, 16 editors
setup.metric: EdiVal-O after the third sequential edit: geometric mean of EdiVal-IF and EdiVal-CC (0-100), the column the table ranks by; stored /100.
setup.protocol: EdiVal-Bench multi-turn editing: each model applies three sequential object-centric edit instructions (T1-T3) per image with default settings (APIs or official repos); EdiVal-IF (instruction following via Qwen2.5-VL-7B plus Grounding DINO checks) and EdiVal-CC (content consistency via DINOv3 features) are combined by geometric mean into EdiVal-O; the table ranks models by EdiVal-O after turn 3.
setup.limitations: Automatic object-centric pipeline (detector + small VLM), not human ratings; turn-1/turn-2 values and the perceptual-quality table (Table 4) are not imported.

setup.version: WEAVEBench as released with arXiv:2511.11434v1 (14 Nov 2025), Table 2
setup.metric: Avg of the Science, Creation, Logic and Game domain scores (GPT-4.1 key-point judge, 0-1).
setup.protocol: WEAVEBench: human-annotated multi-turn, in-context image editing and generation tasks (science, creation, logic, game) requiring visual memory and world knowledge; each editor produces the edited image from the original image and instruction history; GPT-4.1 judges key points against the reference image and the original image (hybrid VLM-judge, validated against three experts); Avg = mean over the four task domains. Editors are run in the partial in-context setting with image-only evaluation (row icons).
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge; benchmark images partly generated by Seedream 4.0, Nano Banana and SeedEdit 3.0; Seedream 4.0 and Nano Banana rows appear twice under different in-context settings and are not imported.

benchmarks.name: Knowledge Visualization T2I (Brief Caption, English overall)

setup.version: Knowledge Visualization benchmark as released with arXiv:2604.22302v1 (24 Apr 2026), Table 2 Brief Caption track
setup.metric: Mean checklist accuracy (Qwen2.5-VL-32B binary VQA) averaged over six subjects, English prompts; %, stored /100.
setup.protocol: Knowledge Visualization benchmark: 1,800 textbook-grounded science prompts (biology, chemistry, geography, history, math, physics; Chinese and English), Brief Caption track (abstract textbook caption, model must supply the knowledge); each image is checked against 4-6 expert-reviewed checklist items by Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct as binary VQA; score = mean item accuracy; 'Overall en' = average over the six subjects on English prompts.
setup.limitations: Single open-weight MLLM judge; Chinese-prompt column and the Detailed Caption track (Table 5) are not imported.

setup.version: RealPref-Bench as released with arXiv:2604.19406v1 (21 Apr 2026), Table 1 'Human' column
setup.metric: Mean human score on the 0-5 rubric (0 = failure, 3 = instruction mostly followed but poor quality, 5 = full compliance with high quality); stored /5.
setup.protocol: RealPref-Bench: real-world images with manually verified edit instructions over eight sub-tasks (add, remove, object swap, background replace, colour, bokeh, relighting, style); user study (Sec. 5.4): five annotators score over 1k edited outputs per the 0-5 rubric (instruction adherence and image quality); 'Human' = average annotator score per model.
setup.limitations: Five annotators; the benchmark was built by the authors of an editing method (HP-Edit, not imported); HP-score columns (VLM scorer) not imported.

setup.version: SWITCH report v5 (7 Jul 2026), Table 3 single-image-to-video block, VLM-as-Judge Overall
setup.metric: Mean Gemini 3.1 Pro overall score on a 1-5 scale per video, stored /5 with chance 0.2.
setup.protocol: SWITCH generative track: image-to-video generation of tangible-interface interactions (e.g. operating light switches, appliance panels) from an initial frame plus a prompt fixing task type, next action, stop condition and required visible evidence; Gemini 3.1 Pro judges each video (1,170 valid evaluations) on scene fidelity, control correctness, procedure correctness and execution observability and gives a direct overall score on a 1-5 scale.
setup.limitations: Single VLM judge; the 160-video human evaluation in the same table reshuffles the ranking and is not imported; video-to-video block not imported. ShareAlike licence.

setup.version: WROP exam, arXiv:2609.28654v1 (23 Sep 2026), Table 2 human preference leaderboard (14 models)
setup.metric: Bradley-Terry Elo from 361 blind pairwise human judgments; 95% CI kept in notes.
setup.protocol: WROP exam: 300 object-permanence questions (six task families); each model receives the conditioning video prefix through its API's interface (true continuation, reference-to-video or frame-wise edit/transfer; Table 1) and its predicted continuation is trimmed to the target span; twenty raters made 361 blind pairwise judgments (50-52 per model, ties 0.5); Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood Elo with one virtual draw per model.
setup.limitations: Small sample (about 52 games per model, wide CIs); models are reached through different API interfaces (continuation, reference-to-video, edit/transfer), so the test mixes capability with interface; ratings relative to this 14-model pool.
